description: Credit card transactions made by European cardholders over two days in September 2013, collected by Worldline and the Machine Learning Group at Universite Libre de Bruxelles (ULB).
applicability_notes: This is the one dataset of the four whose feature set is explicitly, deliberately anonymized past usefulness: V1-V28 are PCA components of the original features and are not individually interpretable, and the dataset card states the original features cannot be released for confidentiality reasons. `Time` and `Amount` are the ONLY two fields with any real-world meaning.

There is no MCC, merchant ID, device ID, or customer ID of any kind published. Categorical cardinality, per-MCC amount comparison, transactions-per-party, and graph degree distribution are ALL structurally not applicable to this dataset -- not merely unavailable in this pass, but genuinely absent from what was ever published.

`Time` is seconds elapsed since the first transaction in the dataset, over a 2-day span; there is no stated calendar epoch, so hour-of-day/day-of-week cannot be derived without an unverifiable assumption about what wall-clock time `Time=0` corresponds to.

Because Time and Amount are the only two usable fields, this dataset can only inform the amount_distribution and (very weakly, via the 2-day/~172,800s span) an order-of-magnitude inter-arrival sanity check -- not a real inter-arrival distribution, since the per-row values are not reproduced here.

fraud_rate.source: Kaggle dataset card states 0.172% positive class directly (492 / 284807).

time_span_days.source: Kaggle dataset card: transactions collected over two days.

amount_currency.source: Dataset card describes European cardholders; amounts commonly treated as EUR in downstream write-ups.

amount_summary.source: Widely repeated summary statistics from public EDA notebooks/tutorials on this exact, very well-known dataset (e.g. describe()-style output reproduced across dozens of independent write-ups). Not printed verbatim on the dataset card itself, so treated as an approximation rather than a primary citation; only used here for scale-invariant shape comparison (skew, tail ratio), not exact value matching.

usable_for_validation_areas: amount_distribution (overall shape only, scale-invariant comparison -- currency and population differ from generated INR data)
not_usable_for: amount_distribution_per_mcc (no MCC field, by design -- PCA-anonymized)
inter_arrival_time (would require raw per-row Time values, which are not reproduced here)
graph_degree_distribution (no party identifiers, hence no graph)
